More than 40 cats were reunited with their owners after the multiday operation last week, but several dozen of those rescued have died due to the harsh conditions in which they were found, the groups said.

euronews.title: School closures, alcohol bans and slow trains: How Europe’s heatwave is shutting down daily life

euronews.description: Thousands gather at Denmark's Fano International Kite Festival as giant dragon, whale and octopus kites fill the skies above the coast.

euronews.description: Germany’s Schleswig-Holstein has launched a digital campus with over 600 online and in-person courses on AI, virtual and augmented reality and other cutting-edge technologies. It is free of charge and open to all.

euronews.title: Canal Saint-Martin becomes cooling spot as heatwave grips Paris
euronews.description: Paris faces extreme heat as crowds use fountains and the Canal Saint-Martin to cool off, while authorities impose alerts and safety measures.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: the promises, the costs and the search for accountability
rfi.description: Ten years on, the UK's decision to leave the European Union is increasingly seen as more than a single referendum result. Critics argue it reflected a wider crisis of political imagination, with Brexit supporters misreading both Britain and the world, while the promised future never arrived.

rfi.title: Repeated errors in handling of rape case linked to French girl's death: report
rfi.description: An administrative investigation ordered after the death of 11 year-old Lyhanna in southern France has revealed serious failings in how a previous rape complaint against the main suspect was handled. The case has brought the French judicial and police system under stark scrutiny, especially regarding cases of child abuse.

rfi.title: 'Poison in your coffee' report sounds alarm over widespread pesticide use
rfi.description: Coffee production around the world depends heavily on pesticides, leaving millions of farm workers exposed to harmful chemicals while pesticide residues are also found in exported coffee beans, a report published on Monday warned.

rfi.title: Paris court rejects bid to reopen probe into Caribbean chlordecone contamination
rfi.description: The Paris appeals court has upheld a decision not to reopen a criminal investigation into the use of chlordecone, a toxic pesticide that has been linked to cancer and other health problems in around 90 percent of the adult population in Guadeloupe and Martinique.

rfi.title: UN warns of an 'imminent risk of mass atrocities' in Sudan's Kordofan
rfi.description: In Sudan, NGOs and the UN have warned of an "imminent risk of mass atrocities" in El-Obeid, a major city in North Kordofan. This comes as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) step up their campaign against the regular army in the region.

rfi.title: France, Germany reach deal on arms maker KNDS, opening door to stock market
rfi.description: France and Germany announced Monday a deal for the joint governance of Amsterdam-headquartered arms maker KNDS, paving the way for a blockbuster share offering as they seek to boost faltering European defence cooperation.

rfi.title: France's scorching weekend heat leads to elderly deaths, spate of drowings
rfi.description: The deaths of three elderly people in southwestern France have been linked to the ongoing heatwave hitting the country, while authorities have reported an increase in drownings, as people seek relief from the heat in rivers and lakes.

rfi.title: UK's Starmer resigns as prime minister
rfi.description: UK leader Keir Starmer announced his resignation on Monday following months of pressure, kickstarting a process that will see Britain get its seventh prime minister in a decade.

rfi.title: DRC announces free healthcare for all illnesses in Ituri as Ebola gains ground
rfi.description: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has announced the introduction of free healthcare for all diseases in Ituri – a pilot project that authorities hope to extend nationwide. This comes as the country struggles to contain an Ebola outbreak, with confirmed cases now at over 1,000.

rfi.title: Ethiopia’s ruling party wins another large majority in parliament
rfi.description: Ethiopia's ruling party has won over 90 percent of seats in parliament, according to official results announced three weeks after the election.

rfi.title: Schools closed as France's heatwave threatens to break records
rfi.description: Hundreds of schools across France will remain closed on Monday and nearly 2,000 are preparing to send pupils home early as the country braces for record temperatures amid a prolonged heatwave.

rfi.title: What is France's heatwave warning system and how does it work?
rfi.description: France is taking emergency measures to cope with a prolonged heatwave, with a record 35 departments placed on maximum red alert. RFI explains how the French system works and what the different alert levels mean in practice.

rfi.title: Poland and Germany renew historic ties to defend Europe's eastern flank
rfi.description: Poland and Germany entered a new era in bilateral relations this week after signing a new defence agreement amid heightened tensions with Russia. It comes 35 years on from a landmark pact that ended decades of enmity and laid the foundations for an increasingly strategic partnership.

rfi.title: Cape Verde boss Bubista targets place in knockout stages after draw with Uruguay
rfi.description: Cape Verde head coach Bubista targeted a place in the knockout rounds of the 2026 World Cup after his tournament debutants fought back to finish 2-2 with Uruguay on Sunday less than a week after they held title favourites Spain to a goalless draw.

rfi.title: Global partnership brings hope amid high pedestrian road deaths in Nairobi
rfi.description: With pedestrians accounting for up to half of road deaths in Kenya, experts say the rapid expansion of the country's capital Nairobi's road network has failed to take into account how many journeys still begin on foot.

rfi.title: 'United front' on slavery reparations after historic summit in Ghana
rfi.description: Countries pushing for reparations for slavery have hailed a milestone after adopting a shared manifesto for reparatory justice at a global summit in Ghana. Participants said the conference had given new momentum to their fight on both sides of the Atlantic.

rfi.title: World Cup's carbon footprint under scrutiny as Fifa boss racks up air miles
rfi.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has been a busy man at this World Cup but his unquenchable thirst to pack in as many matches as possible is causing unrest among environmentalists who are questioning his indifference to climate change.

rfi.title: Middle East war drives up bitumen costs for African road builders
rfi.description: War in the Middle East is pushing up the price of bitumen, the material used to make asphalt and road surfaces – and the effects are being felt across Africa, where few countries produce their own. Higher costs and longer delivery times are forcing firms from Madagascar to Guinea to Cameroon to renegotiate contracts, absorb rising expenses and rethink how they manage supplies.

lemonde.description: Affaiblissement financier et humain, montée des attaques idéologiques, émergence de l’intelligence artificielle… La communauté scientifique est confrontée à de nombreux défis, à l’image du CNRS, victime de restrictions budgétaires. lemonde.title: Ousmane Dembélé, Ballon d’or dans l’ombre de Kylian Mbappé à la Coupe du monde 2026
lemonde.description: Brillant avec le Paris Saint-Germain où il est jugé indispensable, l’attaquant est plus discret quand il évolue avec les Bleus. En difficulté lors du match France-Sénégal, le Ballon d’or 2025 veut inverser la tendance, lundi, face à l’Irak.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les dirigeants des principales puissances militaires européennes se réuniront mercredi à Berlin

lemonde.title: Chlordécone : la cour d’appel de Paris confirme le non-lieu dans le scandale sanitaire de ce pesticide
lemonde.description: Alors que la justice ne souhaite pas poursuivre l’enquête pénale, les victimes du chlordécone expriment un sentiment d’abandon et réclament des réparations concrètes face à un scandale toujours d’actualité.

lemonde.title: Le Groupe EBRA lance un plan de départs volontaires pour réduire les effectifs de 10 %
lemonde.description: La direction du groupe de presse régional de l’est de la France, détenu par le Crédit mutuel, compte supprimer 400 postes sur 3 200. lemonde.title: « Le Meurtre de Rachel Nickell », sur Netflix : seize ans d’enquête et d’erreurs aux conséquences funestes
lemonde.description: Le documentaire revient sur un fait divers de 1992, l’assassinat d’une jeune mère devant son fils de 2 ans dans un parc londonien, qui a parallèlement donné lieu à une série de fiction diffusée sur Netflix.

lemonde.description: La 45ᵉ édition de l’événement s’est déroulée sous une chaleur accablante, avec 35 départements placés en vigilance rouge pour canicule, le plus haut niveau d’alerte.

france24fr.description: Les supporters norvégiens ont envahi Times Square dimanche, reprenant leur célèbre mouvement viking. La Norvège affrontera le Sénégal le 23 juin lors de son deuxième match de poule.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : pourquoi Zelensky lance-t-il un ultimatum à la Biélorussie ?
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, a donné une semaine au dirigeant biélorusse pour démanteler des installations utilisées par la Russie, selon Kiev, pour envoyer des drones contre l’Ukraine. Jusqu’où les autorités ukrainiennes sont-elles prêtes à aller pour tenter de saper le soutien biélorusse à l’effort de guerre russe ?

france24fr.title: Jyeuhair, un artiste sans frontières
france24fr.description: Révélé dans la saison 3 de Nouvelle École, Jyeuhair n’a laissé personne indifférent. Dans la musique depuis ses 13 ans, il a d’abord façonné des prods avant de poser sa voix. Inspiré par Lil Wayne, Eminem ou encore Busta Rhymes, il s’impose aujourd’hui comme un artiste qui bouscule les codes musicaux. Il sort l'EP "J.E.R ERA BLOCK PARTy".

france24fr.title: Ebola en RD Congo : plus de 1 000 cas confirmés
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, l’épidémie d’Ebola poursuit sa progression. Les autorités sanitaires recensent désormais 1 003 cas confirmés et 254 décès, franchissant pour la première fois le seuil des mille contaminations. Les précisions de Mamadou Kaba Barry, chef de mission ALIMA en RD Congo.

france24fr.title: Erbil SC, un club devenu une institution footballistique en Irak
france24fr.description: Ce lundi, la France affronte l’Irak en phase de groupes. Malgré un lourd désavantage dans une poule relevée, cette Coupe du monde reste un événement majeur pour l’Irak, de retour dans la compétition après 40 ans d’absence. Un engouement qui s’étend jusqu’au Kurdistan, dans le nord du pays, où la présence de joueurs issus des minorités nationales est particulièrement suivie.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RD Congo : l'OMS constate une accélération de la transmission
france24fr.description: La transmission de l'épidémie d'Ebola en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) s'accélère, malgré le renforcement des mesures de riposte sanitaire, a indiqué l'Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) vendredi.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : Xenia Fedorova, la porte voix du Kremlin
france24fr.description: Dans le contexte de la guerre en Ukraine, la Russie s’appuie sur des relais médiatiques pour défendre sa version des faits. Parmi eux, Xenia Fedorova, ancienne figure de l’antenne de RT France, aujourd’hui accusée de relayer la propagande du Kremlin. Les explications de Cyrille Amoursky, journaliste franco-russe.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : sur la route de Boston au camp de base de l’équipe de France
france24fr.description: On vous amène dans les coulisses d’une mission #CoupeduMonde, l’événement le plus suivi de la planète. Comment nos journalistes s’organisent sur la route, comment gère-t-on les directs et à quel point les trajets sont longs et périlleux ? Avec @cedferreira au micro

france24fr.title: Avec De la Espriella, les "droites dures" en Amérique latine enregistrent une nouvelle victoire
france24fr.description: Au terme d'un scrutin serré, l'avocat et millionnaire d'ultradroite Abelardo de la Espriella a remporté la présidentielle colombienne face à son rival de gauche, Ivan Cepeda, dimanche. En promettant d'importer le modèle répressif du chef d'État salvadorien Nayib Bukele, il confirme le virage à l'extrême droite de l'Amérique latine. Décryptage de sa victoire.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : L’enthousiasme des supporters irakiens avant le match contre la France
france24fr.description: Vêtus des maillots de leur équipe nationale et agitant des drapeaux à la gloire de leurs pays, les supporters irakiens se sont rassemblés sur les marches de la statue de Rocky, à Philadelphie. L'Irak affrontera la France pour son deuxième match de poule ce lundi.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les supporters français prêts pour France-Irak
france24fr.description: Alors que le deuxième match de poule de la France au Mondial 2026 approche, les supporters des Bleus se sont rassemblés en Philadelphie. Petits et grands rêvent déjà de ramener la coupe à la maison.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : sélectionneur sans contrat, primes non versées… le Sénégal sous tension
france24fr.description: Dans le groupe I, le Sénégal joue déjà gros face à la Norvège. Battus lors de leur premier match après avoir longtemps résisté à l’équipe de France, les Lions de la Teranga n’ont plus de marge d’erreur. En coulisses, plusieurs tensions internes sont évoquées, entre primes non versées et conditions de préparation contestées.

france24fr.title: Royaume-Uni : après la démission de Keir Starmer, la voie libre pour Andy Burnham ?
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre travailliste Keir Starmer a annoncé lundi sa démission après des mois de pression, et son principal rival Andy Burnham semble plus que jamais en position de force pour lui succéder à la tête du Labour et à Downing Street. Les précisions de Catherine Coron, maîtres de conférences en civilisation britannique à l'Université Paris Panthéon-Assas.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : à Erbil, le football irakien porté par ses minorités
france24fr.description: La France affronte l’Irak en match de poules. Dans un groupe relevé, l’équipe irakienne part avec un net désavantage. Battue 4-1 par la Norvège lors de son premier match, elle aborde pourtant cette Coupe du monde comme un événement majeur, près de 40 ans après sa dernière participation. Une qualification vécue comme historique, jusque dans le nord du pays, au Kurdistan, où la présence de joueurs issus des minorités nationales revêt une forte portée symbolique.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la France et l'Argentine visent les 16es, le Cap-Vert continue de rêver
france24fr.description: Après une entrée en lice réussie, la France et l'Argentine ont l'occasion de valider leur billet pour les seizièmes de finale dès leur deuxième match. Une nouvelle occasion pour Kylian Mbappé et Lionel Messi de marquer le Mondial de leur empreinte, respectivement face à l'Irak et l'Autriche.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : quels parcours pour les équipes africaines ? Avec E. Mokolo, A. Bentaha, L. Kabeya
france24fr.description: Victoire de l’Egypte face à la Nouvelle Zélande (3-1), nouveau nul héroïque pour le Cap-Vert avec 2 partout contre l'Uruguay... Que retenir des performances des équipes africaines lors de ce Mondial de football ? Parlons-en avec nos invités, Elton Mokolo, Journaliste sportif à RMC, Winamax Sport, Canal + Afrique, Adel Bentaha, journaliste sportif à So Foot, et Lee-Roy Kabeya, journaliste à Canal + Afrique et L'Équipe.

france24fr.title: EXCLUSIF : reportage à Cuba, un pays paralysé par les pénuries
france24fr.description: Sous la pression de l’administration Trump, le gouvernement cubain a annoncé un vaste paquet de réformes économiques. Une ouverture présentée comme historique, qui s’inscrit dans un processus de libéralisation progressive du régime communiste. Mais sur l’île, la situation reste très dégradée : l’électricité est distribuée au compte-gouttes et l’économie tourne toujours au ralenti, dans un contexte de fortes difficultés quotidiennes. Reportage.

Schwerer Unfall: Bus kracht gegen Laternenmast: zwei Menschen schwer verletzt
Schwimmregeln: Stadtwerke Jena: «Bäder stehen allen Gästen offen»
Fußball-WM 2026: Wetterdienst gibt vor Norwegen – Senegal Hochwasserwarnung aus
zeit.description: Rund um das Stadion in New Jersey gilt heute eine Unwetterwarnung. Schlotterbeck meldet sich zu Wort. US-Amerikanerin leitet letztes deutsches Gruppenspiel. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Forschung: Zu viel Nähe zu China? Sonderprüfung bei Cispa
2. Fußball-Bundesliga: VfL Wolfsburg verpflichtet St. Paulis Wahl
Lebensplanung: Grünen-Fraktionschef Petersdotter kündigt Abschied an
Kriminalität: Tödliche Messerstiche in Bäckerei - Verdächtiger gefasst
Fußball-WM heute: Messi, Mbappé oder noch ein bisschen Klose?
zeit.description: Wem Miroslav Klose seinen Torrekord gönnen würde. Und nach 27 traurigen Sommern: Österreichs Kinder erleben erstmals eine WM.

zeit.title: Hülya Iri: Genossin Iri, wo ist die Million?
zeit.description: Die SPD-Politikerin Hülya Iri soll den Staat um 1,1 Millionen Euro betrogen haben. So raffiniert, dass ihre Partei das lange nicht mitbekam – oder lieber wegsah.

zeit.title: Rücktritt von Keir Starmer: Wer folgt auf Keir Starmer?
zeit.description: Nach anhaltender Kritik räumt der britische Premier Keir Starmer seinen Posten. Wer wird sein Nachfolger? Und: Gewalt, Mobbing und Diskriminierung an Berlins Schulen

zeit.title: Kochgruppe »Azadi«: Der Geschmack von Freiheit
zeit.description: Die Deutsch-Iranerin Farahnaz hat die Küche ihrer ersten Heimat mit in die zweite gebracht, nach Halle. Sie hofft, dass die Gastfreundschaft auf Gegenseitigkeit beruht.

zeit.title: Pflegekosten: 6 Millionen
zeit.description: Sechs Millionen Menschen in Deutschland brauchen Pflege. Was das kostet und wie die Regierung sparen will – ein Überblick in Grafiken.

zeit.title: Krieg um Taiwan: Alles entscheidet sich an der Taiwanfrage
zeit.description: Von außen im Fokus zweier Großmächte, im Innern uneinig – und womöglich der nächste große Konfliktherd. Was in Taiwan auf dem Spiel steht und worum es dabei geht.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die phrasenhaft-erstarrte Reformrhetorik der deutschen Koalition kann weg. Im Moment geht es um bescheidenere Ziele
nzz.description: Anders als früher tönt die Ankündigung von Reformen heute nicht mehr wie eine Verheissung für die Bürger. Das haben sich die Politiker selbst zuzuschreiben.

nzz.title: Der ehemalige Fed-Chef Alan Greenspan ist im Alter von 100 Jahren verstorben
nzz.description: Greenspan leitete die amerikanische Notenbank von 1987 bis 2006 und prägte die amerikanische Geldpolitik fast zwei Jahrzehnte lang.

nzz.title: Zunehmender Hitzestress: Was in den 1970er Jahren ein endloser Sommer war, wäre heute ein sehr kurzer
nzz.description: Eine neue globale Auswertung zeigt: In Europa beginnt starker Hitzestress neuerdings schon Mitte Juni und hält sich bis Ende August.

nzz.title: Hilfe gegen Sex – Ärzte ohne Grenzen entlässt in Tschad 18 Mitarbeiter
nzz.description: Der Skandal ist kein Ausreisser. In den letzten Jahren wurden zahlreiche Missbräuche bei Uno- und Hilfsorganisationen publik. Obwohl viele davon wissen, stossen die Opfer oft auf ein Schweigekartell.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Keir Starmer scheitert an sich selbst – aber vor allem an Grossbritannien
nzz.description: Das Vereinigte Königreich steckt in einer Multikrise. Helfen könnten schmerzhafte Reformen in der Wirtschafts- und Sozialpolitik. Allerdings deutet wenig darauf hin, dass Starmers Nachfolger dazu fähig ist.

nzz.title: Der britische Premierminister Keir Starmer kündigt seinen Rücktritt an
nzz.description: Gerüchte um Starmers angeblich bald anstehenden Rücktritt haben sich in den vergangenen Tagen verdichtet. Nun hat er nach zwei Jahren im Amt einen Rückzug bis September in Aussicht gestellt.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - So teuer ist Ihr Einkauf bei Aldi, Rewe und Co. geworden
nzz.description: Sie haben das Gefühl, alles wird teurer? Vergleichen Sie Ihren Kassenzettel von heute mit dem gleichen Einkauf von 2022 in deutschen Supermärkten – und erleben Sie Ihren persönlichen Preisschock.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: Inspektoren, ein Krisenstab und eingefrorene Guthaben: Auf dem Bürgenstock gab es wenigstens ein bisschen Fortschritt
nzz.description: Nach dem Treffen in der Innerschweiz zeigen sich alle Beteiligten erfreut. Trotzdem gelang bei den Verhandlungen zwischen Iran und Amerika aber kein grosser Durchbruch. Vor allem in Libanon bleibt die Lage angespannt.

nzz.title: Andy Burnham wird voraussichtlich Starmers Nachfolger
nzz.description: Es ist wohl nur noch eine Frage der Zeit, bis Andy Burnham, der bisherige Bürgermeister von Gross-Manchester, den britischen Premierminister ablösen wird. Aber hinter der Labour-Krise steht eine Staatskrise.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Die USA erlauben den Verkauf von iranischem Öl für 60 Tage +++ US-Vizepräsident J. D. Vance spricht über die Verhandlungen mit Iran
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Auf dem Bürgenstock wird nun um ein Ende des Konflikts gerungen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: Jetzt ist klar, mit wem die Zürcher Mitte in die Regierungsratswahlen steigt – es ist ihr Kronfavorit Philipp Kutter. Er sagt: «Ich politisiere bürgerlich»
nzz.description: Die Kleinpartei muss den Sitz der Bildungsdirektorin Silvia Steiner verteidigen. Einfach wird das nicht werden.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Nach dem Unwetter warnt die Stadt vor herabfallenden Ästen – Stadtpräsident Golta äussert sich zum Tod einer Jugendlichen
nzz.description: Die neusten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Der Flughafen Zürich führt neue Regelungen zu Flüssigkeiten ein
Olympische Winterspiele 2038 in der Schweiz: Bundesrat will 200 Millionen Franken bezahlen, verspricht aber, es gebe keine Defizitgarantie
nzz.description: Trotz Geldsorgen kann der Sportminister Martin Pfister bekanntgeben, dass der Bundesrat die Olympischen Spiele finanziell unterstützen will. Für ein Defizit würden Private geradestehen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Waffenruhe im Gazastreifen: Schülerin bei Luftangriff Israels in Gaza getötet
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

observador.title: "Líbano é a grande chave da guerra"
observador.description: Major-General João Vieira Borges aponta Líbano como "chave" para entendimento entre Irão e EUA. Destaca ainda a preponderância da questão nuclear e como qualquer questão pode parar as negociações.

observador.title: A despedida (com final emotivo) de Keir Starmer do Governo
observador.description: Após refletir no campo durante o fim de semana, veio a demissão anunciada. Recordou o orgulho de mudar o partido e o país. Terminou, emocionado, a falar na família. Ficará no cargo até setembro.

observador.title: Imigrantes têm compensado falta de nascimentos
observador.description: INE reviu série desde 2021: população cresceu graças à imigração, que compensou saldo natural negativo. Em 2025, entraram mais 70.862 imigrantes do que saíram.

observador.title: JD Vance: negociações criaram "base sólida" para acordo
observador.description: Reunião em Bürgenstock terminou com "progressos encorajadores". Foram discutidos o Estreito de Ormuz, o cessar-fogo no Líbano e desbloqueio de ativos iranianos.

observador.title: Suspensas sanções dos EUA sobre petróleo iraniano
observador.description: Washington autorizou produção, venda e transporte de hidrocarbonetos iranianos. Decisão publicada no site oficial do Departamento do Tesouro dos EUA.

observador.title: Das ruas à glória: o pastor que virou guarda-redes do Irão
observador.description: O homem que não tinha onde dormir e varria ruas para sobreviver é agora um símbolo para a seleção do Irão. Com um voo frente a De Cuyper, Beiranvand negou o golo à Bélgica e surpreendeu os adeptos.

observador.title: António Costa diz que demissão de Starmer adia cimeira
observador.description: O presidente do Conselho Europeu lamentou a saída de Starmer e disse esperar que o sucessor dê "continuidade" ao relançamento das relações entre a UE e o Reino Unido.

observador.title: Lagarde diz que situação económica da Zona Euro está frágil
observador.description: Lagarde apontou que "as implicações completas da guerra para a inflação e o crescimento no médio prazo dependerão da intensidade e da duração do choque nos preços da energia".

observador.title: B-Rural Summit: pensar o futuro da agricultura
observador.description: É já no dia 23 de junho, em Lisboa, que se realiza o B-Rural Summit 2026. A renovação geracional no setor da agricultura e das florestas é o tema em destaque.

observador.title: Juro dos Certificados de Aforro aumenta em Junho
observador.description: A subida das taxas de juro é uma moeda com outra face. Os produtos de poupança que estão indexados à Euribor ficam mais atraentes. É o caso dos Certificados de Aforro.

observador.title: Treino foi "gatilho" mas não a causa do enfarte de Casillas
observador.description: No julgamento em que Casillas reclama 3,7 milhões ao FC Porto e à Fidelidade, a perita sustentou que a causa primária foi a doença coronária prévia, não o esforço físico.

observador.title: 16h. UE aprova 30 milhões para agricultores portugueses
observador.description: Bruxelas concordou com a fundamentação do Governo português e decidiu atribuir aos agricultores de Portugal a maior fatia do pacote extraordinário de apoio. Ainda, IL quer auditoria urgente à RTP.

observador.title: Delegações deixam a Suíça com roteiro de 60 dias rumo à paz
observador.description: Primeira ronda de negociações entre os Estados Unidos e o Irão na Suíça terminou com "progressos positivos". Ainda, Israel afirma que não tem ambições territoriais no Líbano, mas não vai desmobilizar.

observador.title: Publicado regulamento que define regime de Cibersegurança
observador.description: Regulamento aprova as regras de auto-identificação e respetiva qualificação das entidades e as regras das notificações obrigatórias de incidentes de cibersegurança.

observador.title: Câmara do Porto abre concurso para direção do Cinema Batalha
observador.description: Candidatos têm menos de um mês para se propor ao cargo deixado por Guilherme Blanc, que sai em setembro. Início de funções está previsto para o último trimestre de 2026.

observador.title: Doentes esperam vários meses por fisioterapia no SNS
observador.description: Doentes que sofrem AVC ou que são operados esperam meses. Ordem contesta circuito que implica duas consultas antes da fisioterapia. Convencionados, em dificuldades, pedem melhor pagamento dos atos.

observador.title: Bitcoin: inovação ou especulação
observador.description: Olhamos para o papel da criptomoeda mais conhecida do mundo, o seu impacto no sistema financeiro e os riscos e oportunidades que levanta, com a ajuda de Nuno Lima da Luz e Bernardo Mota Veiga.

observador.title: Undav. Dispensado aos 14, na fábrica aos 17, no topo aos 29
observador.description: O jogador alemão já marcou três golos no Mundial 2026 depois de saltar do banco e igualou um registo de Roger Milla que durava desde 1990. A história de Deniz Undav, o herói improvável de Nagelsmann.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Schock um Nico Schlotterbeck, Tränen bei Keir Starmer, rücksichtslose Radfahrer
spiegel.description: Das verletzte Innenband von Nico Schlotterbeck schockiert Fußball-Deutschland. Der britische Premier rührt sich selbst zu Tränen. Und viele Radler machen einen ratlos. Das ist die Lage am Montagabend.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Überfall auf Geldtransporter – 22-Jähriger zu 14 Jahren Haft verurteilt
spiegel.description: Bei einem Überfall auf einen Geldtransporter in Berlin erbeuteten die Täter 2,4 Millionen Euro. Ein Mann feuerte dabei mit einem Sturmgewehr auf den Wagen. Nun hat ein Gericht mehrere Urteile gefällt.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Frankreich-Spiel droht Absage wegen Unwetter
spiegel.description: Frankreichs Spiel in Philadelphia könnte von heftigem Unwetter betroffen sein. Das Gleiche gilt auch für Norwegen gegen Senegal in New Jersey. Und: DFB-Verteidiger Nico Schlotterbeck fällt aus. Alles Wichtige zum Turnier.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: USA lockern Sanktionen auf iranisches Öl
spiegel.description: Nach »produktiven« Gesprächen mit Teheran setzt Washington Teile seiner Sanktionen vorübergehend aus. Die Maßnahme könnte Iran Milliarden einbringen und die Energiemärkte beruhigen. Die Ölpreise fielen deutlich.

spiegel.title: Australien: Ballista-Spinne jagt Ameisen mit einzigartiger Katapulttechnik
spiegel.description: Forscher aus Greifswald und Australien haben beobachtet, wie eine Spinne besonders wehrhafte Ameisen überlistet. Es handele sich um eines »der leistungsstärksten bekannten Fangsysteme im Tierreich.«

spiegel.title: Bachfest Leipzig: Dirigent John Eliot Gardiner soll Mitarbeiterin bedrängt haben
spiegel.description: Beim Bachfest soll Musiker John Eliot Gardiner versucht haben, einer Frau eine Papierrolle in den Ausschnitt zu stecken. Er entschuldigte sich nach dem Vorfall, wies den Vorwurf eines sexuellen Übergriffs jedoch zurück.

spiegel.title: Äthiopien: Regierungspartei von Abiy Ahmed gewinnt Wahlen deutlich
spiegel.description: Er startete als Hoffnungsträger, erhielt den Friedensnobelpreis – heute ist sein Führungsstil geprägt von Repressionen. Nun hat Abiy Ahmeds Partei die Wahl in Äthiopien gewonnen. Pannen überschatteten den Urnengang.

spiegel.title: Luigi Pantisano: Das ist der Sound vom neuen Linkenchef
spiegel.description: Für seine »Faschismus«-Aussage über die CDU bittet der neue Linkenchef Luigi Pantisano um Entschuldigung. Doch auch im Umgang mit Israel, Kanzler Merz oder AfD-Wählenden agiert er wenig zimperlich. Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Tennis: Markéta Vondroušová nach verweigertem Dopingtest für vier Jahre gesperrt
spiegel.description: Die tschechische Tennisspielerin Markéta Vondroušová kam einer Aufforderung zur Dopingkontrolle nicht nach, sie begründete ihr Verhalten mit einer Angststörung. Geholfen hat ihr das nicht.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Keir Starmer tritt zurück – was von seiner Amtszeit bleibt
spiegel.description: Keir Starmer hatte den Briten Ruhe nach den Brexit-Jahren versprochen. Nun tritt auch er zurück. Was von seiner Amtszeit bleibt und was die Menschen jetzt erwartet.

spiegel.title: Wolfgang Porsche plant Verkauf seiner Villa Paschinger Schlössl in Salzburg
spiegel.description: Salzburgs Bevölkerung hat sich gegen einen geplanten Privattunnel zu Wolfgang Porsches Anwesen gewehrt. Nun gibt der VW-Patriarch offenbar auf. Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen soll das »Paschinger Schlössl« verkauft werden.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Kinder berichten von Beleidigungen, Mobbing und Schlägen in Schulen
spiegel.description: Berlins Bildungssenatorin sieht ein Warnsignal: Eine Studie richtet den Fokus auf Gewalterfahrungen von Kindern in Berlins Schulen. Insbesondere in Grundschulen wächst demnach das Problem.

spiegel.title: Nico Schlotterbeck bei der Fußball-WM 2026: Was das WM-Aus für die Nationalelf bedeutet
spiegel.description: Nico Schlotterbeck hat eine schwere Sprunggelenkverletzung erlitten. Sein Ausfall verändert die Statik der DFB-Elf: Zentral wird nun vor allem ein Spieler – und das ist nicht Antonio Rüdiger.

spiegel.title: Luigi Pantisano: Carsten Linnemann lehnt Entschuldigung ab
spiegel.description: Nach seinem CDU-AfD-Vergleich rudert der neue Linkenchef Luigi Pantisano zurück. Bei CDU-Generalsekretär Carsten Linnemann findet das jedoch keinen Anklang.

spiegel.title: Irina Scherbakowa: »Stalin wollte nicht glauben, dass Deutschland sein Land attackieren würde«
spiegel.description: Ihr Vater überlebte als sowjetischer Soldat die Schlacht um Stalingrad: Hier erklärt Historikerin Irina Scherbakowa die russische Perspektive auf Hitlers Vernichtungskrieg – und wie Putin sie instrumentalisiert.

spiegel.title: Deniz Undav: Warum der DFB-Stürmer von vielen Fans so geliebt wird
spiegel.description: Deniz Undav ist der Liebling der deutschen Fans, für Jesiden ist er eine Identifikationsfigur. Das liegt an seinen Toren. Und daran, dass er so anders ist als das Fußball-Establishment.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: VW-Manager Michael Obrowski wird neuer Finanzchef
spiegel.description: Die letzte Finanzvorständin der Bahn war nur wenige Monate im Amt, jetzt ist ein Nachfolger gefunden. Michael Obrowski arbeitet bislang bei einer Volkswagen-Sparte. Und kennt von dort zwei Eigenheiten der Bahn.

new-sci.description: Putting brain cells into a hibernation-like state via drugs that cool down core body temperature may help to preserve them following a stroke

Most of the time, when they identify spectral features—specific absorption or emission lines from different types of light gathered from a planet, moon or star—these features are known to be caused by certain atoms or molecules. phys-org.title: Does climate change lead to more migration? Here's why researchers can't agree on the evidence
phys-org.description: Images of families displaced by floods, prolonged droughts or extreme storms have become a distressingly regular feature of the daily news. As the impact of climate change intensifies, so does concern over its effects on human mobility. Ongoing changes to the world's climate now raise a salient, apparently simple question: To what extent does climate change cause migration?

phys-org.title: Poo emoji, earthworm castings and pasta all obey the same coiling theory, physicists find
phys-org.description: Ask a child to draw some poo, and the shape will invariably be the same: a coil, broad at the base and pointy at the top, similar to a spiral swirl of soft-serve ice cream. In fact, the often-used poo emoji has this exact shape, as do most actual mounds of feces found in nature. Exceptions occur, though, particularly in the feces of some worms that extrude their excrement "upside down" from the ground. As it turns out, there is remarkable physics behind these differences in poo shapes.

phys-org.title: Third known interstellar visitor 3I/ATLAS may be billions of years older than the solar system, study finds
phys-org.description: An interstellar comet that blazed past the sun last year could be nearly three times older than our solar system and is unlike anything ever seen before in our cosmic backyard, astronomers said Monday.

phys-org.title: Industrial fisheries discarded 80,000 metric tons of fish from 1950 to 2022, study finds
phys-org.description: Destructive fishing practices and inadequate management allowed industrial fisheries operating in the waters of Saint Pierre and Miquelon to dump about 80,000 metric tons of fish back into the ocean from 1950 to 2022, with authorities failing to track the wasteful practice. This is enough fish to fill 32 Olympic-sized pools.

phys-org.title: Heat stress exposure climbed from 16% to 22% worldwide over 50 years, study shows
phys-org.description: The number of people exposed to dangerous heat stress worldwide has risen sharply over the past half-century, propelled by climate change, according to a study released Monday as Europe sweltered through a punishing heat wave.

phys-org.title: The Caspian Sea has lost an area nearly the size of Sicily: Human activities are a major reason why
phys-org.description: The Caspian Sea, the largest inland body of water on Earth, is shrinking. Not fluctuating, not entering another natural cycle, but shrinking.

phys-org.title: Ancient mud drilled from Antarctic ice holds clues to future sea-level rise
phys-org.description: "What goes on in Antarctica doesn't stay in Antarctica—it has global implications," Geology tauira Natalie-Jane Reid says. Reid is one of two Otago Ph.D. candidates who contributed to an Antarctic sediment core workshop at the Otago Repository for Core Analysis (ORCA) held during the first two weeks of June. phys-org.title: Newly described Australian ballista spider builds a spring-loaded snare to catch a single ant species
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers has discovered a remarkable new spider species in the rainforest of North Queensland that spins an ingenious and powerful spring-actuated snare to catch a single species of ant—one ant at a time—in what they describe as "the ultimate specialization."

phys-org.title: Can we predict how fast a bioplastic breaks down? A new AI tool says 'yes'
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Agricultural University of Athens (AUA), a partner in the ANIPH project, published a study that helps predict how quickly biodegradable bioplastics break down in the environment.

phys-org.title: Cryo-EM imaging reveals how a molecular gate lets bulky proteins pass cell membranes intact
phys-org.description: How large, fully folded proteins can pass through cell membranes without destroying them has long been one of the open questions in cell biology. Using cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), Leonid Sazanov and Ziyu Zhao at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) have now uncovered new details about a molecular "gate." Their findings were published in Molecular Cell.

phys-org.title: How oxygen sneaks into a corked wine bottle long before the first pour
phys-org.description: The main reason for sealing wine bottles with a cork is to protect the liquid from oxygen. However, it is not an impermeable barrier, and a small amount of air leaks in, which is not always entirely bad news. The gas helps the wine mature and develop a more complex flavor.

phys-org.title: EU Commission's draft legislation on pesticides: European researchers highlight the risks
phys-org.description: The European Commission has presented a new legislative package. It is intended to reform key provisions that have hitherto governed the approval of pesticides. The "Food and Feed Safety simplification package" is part of a comprehensive strategy through which the Commission aims to simplify legislation in the European Union (EU) and reduce the administrative burden.

phys-org.title: Bow-and-arrow-shaped radio galaxy discovered by citizen scientist
phys-org.description: Astronomers have discovered a "remarkable" bow-and-arrow-shaped radio galaxy with an enormous arc-like structure extending nearly 1.8 million light-years across. The newly identified system, detailed in a new paper published today in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society: Letters, has a "highly unusual" and asymmetric structure unlike those seen in standard radio galaxies.

phys-org.title: Researchers develop antiviral candidate for deadly mosquito-borne brain infections
phys-org.description: Can newly identified antiviral compounds help stop some of the most dangerous mosquito-borne viruses that attack the brain? A research team led by scientists at The University of Alabama in Huntsville (UAH), a part of The University of Alabama System, has generated a new class of antiviral compounds that show strong therapeutic potential against Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), considered the most dangerous neurotropic alphavirus known to infect humans. The study is published in the

phys-org.title: Investigating quantum and molecular plumbing in nanofluidics research
phys-org.description: Our body contains an intricate system of tiny vessels through which blood, water and other molecules flow. When the size of the pipes shrinks to the nanoscale, where only a few molecules can fit side by side, the classical laws of physics governing the behavior of water are influenced by the atomic structure of the walls. phys-org.title: Europe scorched by latest heat wave
phys-org.description: Thirteen people died by drowning in searing temperatures in France over the weekend, with the heat wave set to intensify from Monday across much of Europe, forcing warnings and special measures.

phys-org.title: Marmoset monkeys adapt their voices to sound more like their social partners, study finds
phys-org.description: Many animal species that live in groups are known to adjust their behavior to strengthen their social bonds or increase their coordination with others around them. For instance, humans and some other animals exhibit vocal plasticity, meaning they tend to modify the sounds they produce based on their past experiences and the peers they have interacted with.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: The World Must Adopt an Electrification Roadmap
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Reversing Brexit Is Labour’s Best Hope
proj-syn.description: When it comes to the relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union, political expediency and economic logic both point in the same direction. A majority of British voters now believe that Brexit was a mistake, and they are looking for a leader who will put the issue back on the national agenda.

proj-syn.title: Global Health Reform Must Bolster Innovation
proj-syn.description: As funding falls for global public health, calls for a country-led system have grown louder. Such reforms are necessary, but they must not come at the expense of new vaccines, medicines, and diagnostics, which can be delivered by strengthening mechanisms—such as product development partnerships—that already work.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.

proj-syn.title: White House Fight Night
proj-syn.description: The venue on the South Lawn for UFC Freedom 250 was built, approved, lit, filmed, defended, watched, and enjoyed as part of a celebration of freedom. President Donald Trump’s chosen object to represent that celebration was a cage.

proj-syn.title: The US-Iran Agreement Is a First Step
proj-syn.description: While the recently announced US-Iranian memorandum of understanding is certainly good news, it is not definitive. The path from a statement of diplomatic intent to a fully restored, non-inflationary energy supply chain is fraught with political, technical, and physical risks.
